There are the following definitions in mathlib all related to the concept of an increasing sequence:

  • docs#IsChain - A totally ordered subset of a set. The relation is provided explicitly rather than being typeclass inferred.
  • docs#IsMaxChain - A chain which is not a proper subset of any other chain
  • docs#Flag - Bundled version of IsMaxChain
  • docs#Monotone - A weakly increasing function
  • docs#IsFiltration - A Monotone function F that comes equipped (via outParam) with a function F_lt such that F_lt j = ⨆ i < j, F i. If your codomain is a complete lattice, this is just a monotone function, and if your index set is ℕ and your codomain is a (regular) lattice, this is also just a monotone function. This is defined in a leaf node of mathlib and is never used.
  • docs#Ideal.Filtration - For a fixed ideal I of R and an R-module M: A decreasing sequence of submodules of M s.t. left multiplication by an element of I is contained within the next module.
  • docs#IsRingFiltration and docs#IsModuleFiltration - Not sure what these are, but they are also unused
  • docs#MeasureTheory.Filtration - A monotone function that outputs sigma algebras, where the sigma algebras are contained in the given universal sigma algebra.

Additionally, in pure math there is the notion of a partial flag of a vector space, which is just a strictly monotone sequence of submodules where the first one is ⊥ and the last is ⊤. A complete flag is what mathlib would call a docs#Flag. There's also docs#Module.Basis.flag which is also unused.

I'm not totally sure I understand this organization, as there are a lot of definitions which do similar things. Some are sets, some are functions. Would it be possible to deduplicate these definitions?

The family docs#IsFiltration, docs#IsRingFiltration and docs#IsModuleFiltration were all introduced in anticipation of the definition of the associated graded ring of a filtration (see #33217, which has not moved in a long while though).

I might need the concept of a flag/subspace nest in linear algebra for #Is there code for X? > Singular Value Decomposition. Ideally, we can use the same concept of a flag for things like nest algebras and upper triangular matrices.

I'm not sure using docs#Flag is a good idea, because it isn't indexed by anything (although I suppose there are some advantages to this). What should I do?
There is also this definition from https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~krdavids/Preprints/Davidson_NestAlgebras.pdf. I think the Lat T in this definition corresponds to docs#Module.End.invtSubmodule.
docs#Flag is relevant to abstract polytopes, which are defined so that their automorphism groups is transitive on flags. But I don't think there's been any work on that in years...
Is the current definition of docs#Flag sufficient for those purposes? I feel like in some applications sets are better whereas in others, indexed families are better
That's hard to say without any actual code. I think @ooovi was thinking about this a while back.
